reference: kemiller2002/limen#40 (LCP-034; defect found proving the outbox; the rule that OutcomeUnknown is never collapsed into Failure)
placement: Core (kernel mechanism + contract, protocol 1.4). Verified in Chromium: when a connection drops after a POST reached the server, fetch rejects with TypeError (and Chromium may already have resent it), and the kernel reported Failure{network}, documented as retryable: an unknown outcome collapsed into a confident failure. Only the one fetch call can classify this, so no pack can fix it. The fix: for POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE, a thrown fetch while the browser was online is OutcomeUnknown{connection-lost}; safe methods, and any request made while navigator.onLine is false, stay Failure{network}. A 1.3 engine cannot decode the new reason, so it hears OutcomeUnknown{timeout-after-dispatch}: the outcome kept safe, the reason approximated and documented. Retry stays the engine's.
